subject: amateur youtube influencers
one_liner: Payments infrastructure for channels with fewer subscribers than a cul-de-sac.
brand_voice_notes: Stripe-grade fintech seriousness applied to sums under four dollars. Every number is real and small and presented with enormous ceremony. Never acknowledge that the amounts are tiny. Thumbnail tropes (red circles, arrows, shocked faces) are used as if they were standard financial annotation.

hero.h1: Accept payments from all 41 of your subscribers.
hero.sub: Ding. is the financial stack behind the internet's least-watched creators. Tips, brand deals and merch, settled to your bank in amounts we are legally required to display.

features.title: Micro-Payouts
features.blurb: We move your $0.14 of ad revenue to your checking account across nine business days, then itemize the $0.30 fee so you can see exactly where it went.

features.title: Sponsor Checkout
features.blurb: A hosted checkout page for brand deals, pre-filled with your uncle's gutter company. Supports net-90 terms, payment in gift cards, and exposure.

features.title: Radar for Views
features.blurb: Fraud detection that notices when one IP address in Ohio watched your video 212 times. We flag it, refund it, and notify your mother.

demo_screen_concept: A Stripe-style creator payments dashboard for the channel 'KayleighCooksSometimes': a gross-volume card ($3.41 this month, up from $0.00, shown as +∞%), a balance card with a progress bar toward the $100 payout threshold and an ETA of 2031, a filterable and searchable payments table (Super Thanks, one sponsor deal, one mug of merch) with status pills Succeeded / Pending / Disputed / Refunded by Mom. Clicking a row opens a detail drawer with payer, fee breakdown and a Radar risk score. A test-mode toggle multiplies every number by 1,000 and adds a banner saying none of it is real. A 'Request payout' button runs a fake progress sequence and ends in a polite decline for being under the threshold.

images.rationale: Hero earns a photo: the composition is a fake video thumbnail and the shocked creator face is the joke. Demo is a payments dashboard (tables, charts), not photo-shaped, so no demo assets. Remaining budget on 3 testimonial headshots.

items.prompt: Editorial photograph styled like an amateur YouTube video thumbnail: a single man in his late twenties in a bedroom home studio, mouth open in exaggerated shock, both hands on his cheeks, ring light, plain grey hoodie, left third of frame; bubblegum pink wall #FDF2F8, orange #EA580C rim light, hot pink #DB2777 glow. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks or UI.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a heavyset man in his forties with a goatee and plain black t-shirt holding a sealed cardboard box; pale pink #FDF2F8 seamless, hot pink #DB2777 edge light. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks or UI.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a woman in her early thirties with a messy bun and flour-dusted apron holding a wooden spoon like a microphone; pale pink #FDF2F8 seamless, hot pink #DB2777 edge light. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks or UI.

Deadpan corporate headshot of a lanky seventeen-year-old with a gaming headset around his neck and a dark hoodie, unsmiling; pale pink #FDF2F8 seamless, hot pink #DB2777 edge light. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks or UI.

design_direction.style: Thumbnail-shock fintech, creator-pink daylight mode. Stripe-docs restraint (thin rules, mono figures, generous whitespace) defaced with YouTube thumbnail annotation: hand-drawn red circles around dollar amounts, fat red arrows, yellow highlighter blocks, outlined all-caps headline type with a hard drop shadow. Treated as normal financial markup.

fonts.body: 'Fira Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Real-time / operations fintech landing (hero with live product preview, metrics strip, features, social proof, pricing)
design_direction.motion_vocab: Red annotation circles draw themselves in via SVG stroke-dashoffset when they enter view; figures tick up from 0.00 to their tiny final value; a notification-bell 'ding' wobble on the CTA hover. All gated by prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero. Left: Anton headline in ink with a pink hard shadow, the number 41 circled in red SVG. Right: a fake video thumbnail card (16:9) using hero.webp, a shocked creator, with an HTML overlay of a giant yellow-boxed '$0.14' and a red arrow pointing at it, then a small Stripe-style payment confirmation toast pinned under it. Below: a thin mono metrics strip (Median payout $0.38, Average settlement 9 business days, Subscribers served 41).
